Description.Name: Bagele's Ride
Description.Details: Commander, remember those pirates we worked with on {TGT_SYSTEM.name}?" You nod cautiously. "Well, apparently they've been digging through the loot after our little raid. One of their bosses just contacted me with a rather unusual offer." Darius hands over a holocom. The screen flickers to life, revealing a grinning pirate standing in front of a battered but unmistakably customized Hatchetman."Commander!" the pirate says enthusiastically. "Pleasure doing business with you. While sorting through that depot, we found this beauty tucked away in a maintenance hangar. Custom work all over it. Whoever owned it spent a lot of money making it special." Before the pirate can continue, a voice erupts from behind you."THAT'S MINE!" You turn to find Bagele practically sprinting across the command deck. The MechWarrior nearly snatches the holocom from your hands. "Commander, that's my Hatchetman! I told you about it when I signed on! I lost it years ago during a retreat gone bad. Look at the shoulder plating—the custom armor pattern. The reinforced hatchet mount. That's my machine!" On the holocom, the pirate glances between you and Bagele, his grin widening. "Well, that certainly makes things interesting." Bagele looks at you desperately. "Commander, please. That's my ride. I've spent years trying to track it down." The pirate clears his throat."Now, now. Let's talk business." The image zooms in on the Hatchetman. "Finding this machine wasn't free. Recovering it wasn't free. Convincing my associates not to strip it for parts definitely wasn't free." You already know where this is going. "Three million C-Bills," the pirate says cheerfully. "And the Hatchetman is yours. Fully intact. We even promise not to remove anything important before delivery." Bagele's face falls. "Three million?!" The pirate shrugs. "Sentimental value is expensive." Bagele turns back toward you, looking equal parts embarrassed and hopeful. "Commander... I know it's a ridiculous amount of money. But that's my machine. In my hands, you won't regret it!" The pirate's grin returns."So, Commander. Three million C-Bills. One customized Hatchetman. What's it going to be?"

Description.Name: Acceptance.
Description.Details:
You look from the holocom to Bagele and back again. Three million C-Bills is a ridiculous amount for a salvaged Hatchetman. Then again, this isn't just a Hatchetman.

You sigh. "Three million. Not one C-Bill more."

The pirate's grin immediately widens. "Commander, I knew you were a visionary."

Bagele looks like he's about to collapse from relief. "Really? You're buying it?"

You nod. "You're lucky I value experienced MechWarriors more than I value my accounting reports."

The pirate laughs. "A pleasure doing business with you. I'll have my people prepare the transfer immediately."

Bagele grabs the holocom and stares at the image of the Hatchetman. "I never thought I'd see it again."

The pirate points a finger toward the camera.

"We'll get her loaded up and she'll be delivered before the day ends. No missing parts. No surprises." He pauses. "Well... no surprises that weren't already installed when we found her."

The transmission ends.

Bagele turns to you, visibly overwhelmed. "Commander... thank you."

For the first time since meeting him, he looks genuinely happy.

Description.Name: Need More Time.
Description.Details:
You cross your arms. "Three million isn't happening today."

 The pirate visibly deflates. "Ah. One of those conversations."

 "It doesn't mean no," you continue. "It means not yet."

 The pirate considers that for a moment. "Hmmm."

 Bagele immediately steps forward. "Commander, you're still considering it?"

 "I'm considering it."

 The pirate scratches at his beard. "Well, that's unfortunate."

 "Why?" you ask.

 "Storage costs."

 You narrow your eyes. "Storage costs."

 "Storage costs," the pirate repeats confidently. "Hangar fees. Security. Preservation. Regular polishing. Keeping my crew from stealing pieces off it."

 Bagele groans. "You're making that up."

 The pirate ignores him. "Every day that Hatchetman remains in my possession costs money."

 "How much?" you ask. The pirate smiles. "Enough... if you want me to hold it, Commander, the price remains three million for... let's say the next 30 days or so. But eventually there'll be storage fees. Care costs. Administrative costs. Anti-theft costs."

 "Those aren't real costs." Bagele blurts.

 The pirate shrugs, "They become real when I write them down. Take your time. Just don't take too much time."

 The transmission ends, leaving Bagele staring anxiously at you.

Description.Name: Not Interested.
Description.Details:
You don't hesitate. "No."

 The pirate blinks. "No?"

 "No. Three million C-Bills for a salvaged Hatchetman is absurd."

 The pirate looks genuinely disappointed. "I was hoping sentimentality would help close the deal."

 Bagele's face falls. "Commander..."

 You shake your head. "The answer is final."

 The pirate sighs dramatically. "A tragedy."

 "No," you reply. "A business decision."

 The pirate nods reluctantly. "Fair enough. Can't fault a commander for knowing where the line is."

 Bagele looks away from the screen, unable to hide his disappointment. The pirate notices. "Sorry, friend. Looks like your reunion wasn't meant to be."

 The transmission terminates. The screen goes dark. Silence hangs over the command deck.

 Bagele stares at the blank display for several moments before finally speaking. "...Understood, Commander."

 The words are professional. The disappointment behind them isn't.
